title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy Of Music on 1972-03-21

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1972 show with historic first performances and solid playing, captured on a soundboard SBD that has hum and channel quirks but is overall listenable.
ai_review.review: The concert is praised for its playful, focused musicianship – standout moments include the debut of “Looks Like Rain” (Garcia on pedal steel), the first “Stranger”, an epic Truckin’ > The Other One stretch, and a hyper‑charged “One More Saturday Night”.  The SBD source sounds good after modest hum reduction and EQ, though it suffers from occasional buzz, clipped starts and a missing Chinatown track.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple detailed 5‑star reviews highlight an exceptional performance with many historic firsts; recording is solid soundboard but needs minor cleaning, leading to a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hum/buzz present in parts, some clipped track beginnings and missing Chinatown segment; channels need swapping and modest EQ/pitch correction. Reviewers note the SBD is clearer than most and improves with simple hum‑reduction.

standout_songs: Greatest Story Ever Told (first great arrangement)
Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad
poor_songs: Some short songs in second set (noted as less engaging)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set runs nearly two hours with early‑era '72 material and several first‑time debuts; second set builds into a long Truckin’ > The Other One sequence and finishes with an upbeat Saturday Night, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s pedal steel on “Looks Like Rain” is called ‘utterly sublime’; his solo ending on “Greatest Story Ever Told” is highlighted.
band_member_comments.Bob: "Bobby's rhythm is incredible" (praise for Bob Weir’s rhythm guitar throughout the set).
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (keyboardist) disappears from the mix during Chinatown and most of the set; channels need swapping.
band_member_comments.Drums: One reviewer notes they "didn't discern drumming during drums", indicating a weak drum presence in parts.
